4.43 Marine Fishery. Since there would be no additional water releases from Falcon Reservoir, there should not be any net effect upon the lower Laguna Madre marine fishery.
4.44 Historical and Archeological Resources. Although the Amistad area has sites of historical significance, a review of the February 10, 1976 (updated through July 6, 1976) National Register of Historic Places indicates that no properties in the register will be affected by the proposed action, and no properties with recognized potential for such designation are known to be affected by the proposed project.
4.45 There are no known archeological sites of Federal, State, or local significance that will be adversely affected by the operational phase of the proposed project.
4.46 Socioeconomic Considerations. Mounting electrical demand, sharply rising costs, and changing social values have combined to place unusual stresses on the United States electric power industry. Deterioration of the quality of electrical service would of itself and through its economic repercussion degrade our national life. The installation of hydroelectric power at Amistad Reservoir would aid in meeting industrial, commercial, and public energy need, as well as increase the energy self sufficiency of the United States.
4.47 Amistad's proposed hydroelectric operation would add approximately 281.8 million kWh annually to the regional power system. The integrated operation of Amistad and Falcon Reservoirs would also result in an additional 600,000 kWh produced annually at Falcon Reservoir. This increase in percentage of time with monthly Amistad outflows suggests it will enhance the hydroelectric generation of the Eagle Pass plant. However, the release rates of up to 4,000 cfs by the United States plant and up to 9,000 cfs with both plants will have flows exceeding the Maverick Canal capacity, pass the diversion, and not be available for hydroelectric generation.
